deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 13% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 83% last year; 110%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 81% (3 years ago 47%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $81 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 84% (3 years ago 38%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $3.2B, up 68% from a year ago — about 1% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $6.4B, up 215% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 127% vs quarterly sales up 106% (days to collect 54 → 60). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 110%/yr over 3 years and 69%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 65% vs a 5-year range of 16–65% (median 56%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
